name: Iouaridene Dinosaur Footprints
hero_subtitle: Preserved sauropod tracks in High Atlas rock — part of the M'Goun UNESCO Geopark.

overview.title: Walking in the footsteps of dinosaurs
overview.p1: At Iouaridene, fossilised sauropod footprints are preserved in rock layers of the High Atlas. The site is part of the M'Goun UNESCO Global Geopark.
overview.p2: It is a unique stop for geology and family interest, best combined with the Azilal geopark museum for context.
overview.p3: Wear sturdy shoes; access can involve uneven ground. A local guide helps locate the best tracks.

food.title: Where to eat near Iouaridene
food.p1: There are few facilities on site. Eat in Azilal town or at a stop on the way; bring water and snacks for the visit.
food.li1: Cafés and simple restaurants in Azilal town
food.li2: Carry water and a snack for the site itself
food.li3: Museum area may have limited refreshments
food.li4: Plan lunch before or after the footprints visit
food.li5: Cash is useful for small local places

q1.question: How much time for Iouaridene Dinosaur Footprints?
q1.answer: Plan at least the duration indicated in the info box; longer stays reward hikers.

q2.question: Is it suitable for children?
q2.answer: Yes with supervision on paths and near water or cliffs.

q3.question: Do I need a guide?
q3.answer: Not always required, but recommended for valleys and remote tracks.

q4.question: How to get there?
q4.answer: By road from Azilal, Marrakech or Beni Mellal; 4x4 helpful on some mountain roads.
